data.why: The repo ships its own example MRI volume (a teddy-bear phantom scan, uint8) used in the project's own demos/tests; it is a small, already-correctly-formatted NIfTI (.nii.gz) the viewer expects, so no synthetic data is needed.

goals: Load a raw MRI NIfTI volume and inspect its voxel/world orientation to see whether it is already aligned to stereotaxic planes
Manually rotate and translate the volume in the three orthogonal views until anatomical axes (superior/inferior, anterior/posterior, left/right) are aligned
Define and adjust a crop (selection) box to remove non-tissue background space around the brain
Save the resulting rotation/affine matrix so the reorientation can be reproduced later in a scripted pipeline
Save the selection box and export the final reoriented, cropped NIfTI volume for downstream analysis
Reload a previously saved rotation matrix or selection box and append further adjustments on top of it

review.summary: The tree shows the tool's reorient, crop and export workflow faithfully, in sensible phases, with general labels free of tool names, and almost all of the 10 screens checked match their nodes. It needs fixes before filing: it leaves out the load/append-to-resume path and the reorient.py replay that the README stresses, it miscites one screen (025), and it overclaims that the views stay linked while slicing.
